You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE Highschooler (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    grade INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Friend (
    student_id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    friend_id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (student_id, friend_id),
    UNIQUE (student_id, friend_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (friend_id) REFERENCES Highschooler(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES Highschooler(ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Likes (
    student_id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    liked_id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    PRIMARY KEY (student_id, liked_id),
    UNIQUE (student_id, liked_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES Highschooler(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (liked_id) REFERENCES Highschooler(ID)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Do you mean "cool" by name, or by popularity (most friends / most likes), or just want to see all highschoolers? Here are a few common interpretations — pick the one you want or tell me what “cool” means for you.

- All highschoolers
- Names containing the word "cool" (case-insensitive)
- Top 10 most liked (most likes received)
- Top 10 most connected (most friend links)

```sql
-- 1) All highschoolers
SELECT * FROM Highschooler;

-- 2) Names containing "cool" (case-insensitive)
SELECT * FROM Highschooler
WHERE LOWER(name) LIKE '%cool%';

-- 3) Top 10 most liked (most likes received)
SELECT h.ID, h.name, h.grade, COUNT(l.student_id) AS likes_received
FROM Highschooler h
LEFT JOIN Likes l ON h.ID = l.liked_id
GROUP BY h.ID, h.name, h.grade
ORDER BY likes_received DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- 4) Top 10 most connected (counting Friend rows where the student appears as student_id or friend_id)
SELECT h.ID, h.name, h.grade, COUNT(f.student_id) AS friends_count
FROM Highschooler h
LEFT JOIN Friend f ON (h.ID = f.student_id OR h.ID = f.friend_id)
GROUP BY h.ID, h.name, h.grade
ORDER BY friends_count DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

Which of these do you want run, or do you have a different definition of "cool"?
focus on high schoolers who have friends

This lists highschoolers who appear in the Friend table (either as student_id or friend_id), with a count of distinct friends, ordered by friend count:

```sql
SELECT h.ID, h.name, h.grade,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ID = f.student_id THEN f.friend_id ELSE f.student_id END) AS friends_count
FROM Highschooler h
JOIN Friend f ON (h.ID = f.student_id OR h.ID = f.friend_id)
GROUP BY h.ID, h.name, h.grade
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ID = f.student_id THEN f.friend_id ELSE f.student_id END) > 0
ORDER BY friends_count DESC;
```
Also, I want high schoolers who are liked by someone else too.

Here's a query that returns highschoolers who have at least one friend and are liked by someone else (excluding self-likes), with counts of distinct friends and distinct likers, ordered by friend count then likes:

```sql
SELECT h.ID, h.name, h.grade,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ID = f.student_id THEN f.friend_id ELSE f.student_id END) AS friends_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.student_id) AS likes_received
FROM Highschooler h
LEFT JOIN Friend f ON (h.ID = f.student_id OR h.ID = f.friend_id)
LEFT JOIN Likes l ON (h.ID = l.liked_id AND l.student_id <> h.ID)
GROUP BY h.ID, h.name, h.grade
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ID = f.student_id THEN f.friend_id ELSE f.student_id END) > 0
   AND COUNT(DISTINCT l.student_id) > 0
ORDER BY friends_count DESC, likes_received DESC;
```
also want the ids of those high schoolers who fit these criteria

This returns highschoolers (including their ID) who have at least one friend and are liked by someone else, with counts and comma-separated lists of friend IDs and liker IDs:

```sql
SELECT h.ID, h.name, h.grade,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ID = f.student_id THEN f.friend_id ELSE f.student_id END) AS friends_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.student_id) AS likes_received,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ID = f.student_id THEN f.friend_id ELSE f.student_id END) AS friend_ids,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT l.student_id) AS liker_ids
FROM Highschooler h
LEFT JOIN Friend f ON (h.ID = f.student_id OR h.ID = f.friend_id)
LEFT JOIN Likes l ON (h.ID = l.liked_id AND l.student_id <> h.ID)
GROUP BY h.ID, h.name, h.grade
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN h.ID = f.student_id THEN f.friend_id ELSE f.student_id END) > 0
   AND COUNT(DISTINCT l.student_id) > 0
ORDER BY friends_count DESC, likes_received DESC;
```
